QF.id: SIA Social Impact Assessment and Assessors_27

question.text: Impact Assessment Evidence under Section 5.8 can take which forms?

answer.text: Only physical and analytical — oral evidence is explicitly excluded for SSE work

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 5.8 lists four types of impact assessment evidence: Documentary (reports, notes), Oral (discussions with stakeholders), Physical (asset inspection), and Analytical (derived via comparisons, calculations, relationships). All four are valid and complementary. The Trap: A and B incorrectly narrow the evidence set. D confuses SIA with financial audit. Oral evidence is explicitly recognised — note the SIA must record inconsistencies. Cross-Exam Context: Four-fold evidence taxonomy is standard in ICAI audit literature (and overlaps with financial-audit evidence types); XXIII applies the same framework to social programs. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Always corroborate oral evidence (beneficiary testimonies) with at least one documentary or physical piece — a stand-alone testimony without triangulation is the weakest form of SIA evidence under SAS framework.
